article.headline: DreamX compresses a video transition into four action tokens
article.lead: DreamX uses a pretrained video diffusion model to isolate changes that describe an action. Wonder 4 faces a different allocation problem in image restoration: it selects five of thirteen experts per block for each patch.

paragraphs.text: DreamX repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model to enhance latent action learning. It compresses video frames from 1,200 to just 4 tokens, effectively disentangling action-relevant dynamics from visual variations. This method facilitates zero-shot action transfer across different embodiments and environments, achieving state-of-the-art results on the LARY-Bench benchmark. Additionally, the shared latent action interface allows for efficient policy learning, significantly lowering the computational costs associated with video-diffusion-based policies.

Wonder 4 introduces a novel mixture-of-experts (MoE) model for simultaneous image quality enhancement, effectively addressing multiple defects in photographs by employing 13 experts per block and routing image patches to 5 selected experts without the need for degradation classifiers or task labels.

Diffusion Plug-in Priors for Self-Supervised Ultrasound Video Restoration — The paper introduces UltraDiff, a novel approach for self-supervised restoration of ultrasound videos that leverages a frozen pre-trained diffusion model as a plug-in prior, achieving a PSNR improvement of 1.24 dB over the strongest baseline on EchoNet-LVH videos.

From Natural Images to Medical Scans — This paper demonstrates that initializing diffusion models with natural images significantly enhances medical image generation, achieving a 21-34% improvement in generation quality as measured by relative gFID in pixel space, compared to only 14% in latent space.

FlowTranslator introduces a training-free framework for in-image machine translation (IIMT) that leverages advanced text-to-image diffusion models, achieving significant performance improvements over traditional training-based methods.
VidUEU-Agent introduces an automated pipeline for synthesizing high-quality instruction data from raw videos, addressing the challenges of multimodal learning.
Möbius introduces a unified motion-language model that integrates understanding, generation, and editing of human motion within a single framework, eliminating the need for separate modules.

RoboTryOn introduces a novel approach for synthesizing robot demonstrations from human videos by treating the human-to-robot translation as a virtual try-on process, achieving a significant improvement in task performance.

Low-Density 3D Point Cloud Classification — The paper introduces LD-PointNet++, a novel architecture specifically designed for classifying low-density 3D point clouds, addressing performance declines observed in existing methods under such conditions.

Visibility-Aware Reference Generation for Benchmarking Visual 3D Reconstruction in Vegetation-Rich Environments — The paper presents a novel LiDAR-based reference-generation pipeline that enhances the evaluation of visual 3D reconstruction in vegetation-rich environments by generating per-view depth maps and visible reference point clouds from existing datasets.

Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval — The paper introduces Factorized MLLM Embeddings (FactEmbed), which enhances Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) by decoupling compositional query comprehension from the creation of discriminative embeddings.

Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models — The paper introduces UniForget, a novel approach for cross-pathway concept unlearning in unified multimodal models (UMMs), achieving joint forgetting rates of 80.0% on BAGEL-7B-MoT and 92.7% on Janus-Pro-7B.

Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher — The paper introduces Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-Distillation (MTA-OPSD), a novel method that allows each token in a response to select its preferred teacher from a multi-teacher pool, addressing the limitations of fixed teacher models in existing approaches.

picks.question: When the camera and subject move together, which parts of that change survive in the four action tokens?
